mentions.name: laboratory.love
mentions.description: Independent lab testing service for everyday food products, screening for plastic chemicals (phthalates and bisphenols) and publishing all results publicly. Runs as a direct paid service (pay and get published results in a couple of weeks) plus a crowdfunding model where users nominate a product and chip in toward its testing goal, with automatic refunds if a target isn't hit within a year. Funded products are bought anonymously through normal retail across different production lots, and an ISO 17025-accredited lab runs GC-MS with isotope dilution. Also developing a consumption-weighted model showing testing ~100 high-volume grocery SKUs would cover roughly 40% of the packaged food Americans eat by mass.
mentions.problem: Plastic chemicals like phthalates and bisphenols are known or suspected endocrine disruptors, companies aren't required to disclose them, and the science is moving fast (the EU cut its "safe" BPA limit by 20,000x in 2023); independent testing of the kind PlasticList started needed a way to keep happening.
mentions.audience: Explicitly aimed at everyday consumers: it tests everyday food products and publishes all results publicly, with a consumption-weighted plan to test the ~100 grocery SKUs covering roughly 40% of packaged food Americans eat.
mentions.source_excerpt: laboratory.love — independent lab testing of everyday food products for plastic chemicals (phthalates + bisphenols), with all results published publicly. I got nerd-sniped by PlasticList and wanted this kind of testing to keep happening.
